questions.question: How would you implement exactly-once processing in a data pipeline when both source (Kafka) and sink (database) can fail, ensuring no duplicate data or data loss?
questions.answer: Use Kafka transactions with idempotent producers + database transaction IDs + offset commits in atomic transaction.
questions.diagram:
graph TD
    A[Kafka Topic] --> B[Consumer Poll]
    B --> C[Begin Transaction]
    C --> D[Process Records]
    D --> E[Database UPSERT with TxID]
    E --> F{Success?}
    F -->|Yes| G[Send Offsets to Transaction]
    F -->|No| H[Abort Transaction]
    G --> I[Commit Transaction]
    H --> J[Retry Processing]
    I --> K[Next Poll]
    J --> B

questions.question: How would you design a data pipeline that handles both batch and streaming workloads for real-time analytics?
questions.answer: Lambda architecture using batch layer for historical accuracy and speed layer for real-time insights, combined through serving layer.
questions.explanation:
## Why Asked
Tests understanding of modern data architecture patterns and handling multiple processing paradigms
## Key Concepts
Lambda architecture, batch processing, stream processing, data consistency, real-time analytics
## Code Example
```
// Stream processing example (Apache Flink)
DataStream<Event> stream = env.addSource(kafkaSource);
stream.window(TumblingProcessingTimeWindows.of(Time.minutes(5)))
      .aggregate(new CountAggregate())
      .addSink(sink);
```

    A --> C[Speed Layer]
    B --> D[Batch View]
    C --> E[Real-time View]
    D --> F[Serving Layer]
    E --> F
    F --> G[Analytics/Queries]
questions.eli5: Imagine you have two ways to make lemonade at your lemonade stand! One way is making big batches in the morning (that's your batch processing) - you mix everything perfectly and it tastes great. The other way is making fresh cups one by one as friends arrive (that's your streaming) - super fast but maybe not as perfect. The smart trick is having both! You serve the fresh cups right away for instant refreshment, but you also have your perfect batch ready for when someone wants the best-tasting lemonade. Your brain keeps track of both - you know who got fresh cups now and who will get the perfect batch later. That way, everyone gets lemonade exactly when they need it, and you can tell your parents exactly how much you sold today!

questions.question: How would you design a Kafka Streams application to handle exactly-once processing with stateful aggregations while maintaining sub-second latency during traffic spikes?
questions.answer: Use EOS with transactional producer, compacted topics for state, and adaptive processing with standby replicas.
questions.explanation:
## Concept Overview
Exactly-once semantics (EOS) in Kafka Streams ensures no duplicate processing during failures. Stateful aggregations require careful state management and recovery mechanisms.

## Implementation Details
- Enable `processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2`
- Use `KTable` with log compaction for state stores
- Configure standby replicas for fast failover
- Implement custom partitioner for key distribution
- Set appropriate `cache.max.bytes.buffering`

## Code Example
```java
Properties props = new Properties();
props.put(StreamsConfig.PROCESSING_GUARANTEE_CONFIG, StreamsConfig.EXACTLY_ONCE_V2);
props.put(StreamsConfig.NUM_STANDBY_REPLICAS_CONFIG, 1);
props.put(StreamsConfig.CACHE_MAX_BYTES_BUFFERING_CONFIG, 10 * 1024 * 1024);

KStream<String, Event> stream = builder.stream("events");
KTable<String, Long> aggregated = stream.groupByKey()
    .aggregate(
        () -> 0L,
        (key, event, agg) -> agg + event.getValue(),
        Materialized.<String, Long, KeyValueStore<Bytes, byte[]>>as("aggregated-store")
            .withKeySerde(Serdes.String())
            .withValueSerde(Serdes.Long())
            .withLoggingEnabled(Configs.EMPTY)
    );
```

## Common Pitfalls
- Large state stores causing slow recovery
- Improper key distribution leading to hot partitions
- Insufficient memory for state store caching
- Network partitions causing duplicate processing
- Consumer lag during traffic spikes
